chapter: Jelly Roll's road trip, Benny Carter and Chick Webb
title: How Chick Webb assembled his trumpet section and band
summary: Webb built the band from scratch, putting Shelton Hemphill with Louis Hunt and Louis Bacon, with John Trueheart on guitar; Procope says he has no stories.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Is there anything during that period with Chick Webb? Any experiences that might be of interest?

Well, I don't know. Not really. We were playing -- well, I always -- getting back to Chick, he picked the men for this band, like I said, he made the band up from scratch. He didn't -- and I always remember the trumpet players he had. He had Shelton Hemphill, who came to New York with Horace Henderson's band, and of course you know Horace

was -- sometimes he was doing -- working, and sometimes he wasn't. So Chick went to Shelton Hemphill, we used to call him ScaK, ScaK Hemphill, and he got him to play one trumpet. Then he went down to a dancing school, Melody Gardens or something like that, and hired the two trumpet players who were in the dancing school, which were Louis Hunt and Louis Bacon, and he put the three of them together and he had a wonderful trumpet section. Yeah. That's the way he put them together like that, and it worked beautifully. And this is the --
-- the other people in the band, the bass player, and of course John Trueheart was playing banjo and guitar, and so on and so forth.
But I don't remember any stories. I'm not much on stories.
